description.narrative:
The Dutch SRHR Alliance is a two-and-a-half-year pilot partnership (2026–2028) bringing together 11 organizations committed to advancing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), resilient health systems, and inclusive youth participation across multiple countries. At the time of proposal development, the activities planned for the Burkina Faso football club were budgeted at €3,640,582.
The Alliance seeks to protect and strengthen SRHR in a global context characterized by shrinking developmentfunding, increasing anti-rights movements, and weakened health systems. Together with implementing partners in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Mali, Niger, and Uganda, the Alliance responds to the urgent need for sustained investment in SRHR and stronger, more resilient health systems. Investing in fair play is both a commitment to human rights and a strategic approach to achieving sustainable social impact.
All 11 members of the Dutch SRHR Alliance contribute significant value to the partnership through governance, programmeimplementation, learning, and knowledge exchange. Key organizations including Amref, Oxfam Novib, and Wemos provide central management roles, while Hivos, Rutgers, Liliane Fonds, Amref, and Plan International support country-level coordination and mentorship. Choice plays a leading role in strengthening Meaningful and Inclusive Youth Participation across the Alliance’s governance structures.
In addition, organizations such as CoC, VSO, and Aidsfonds contribute technical expertise through participation in knowledge exchange meetings, learning sessions, and collaborative activities coordinated by the Alliance Hub. The partnership emphasizes shared learning, innovation, and cross-country collaboration to strengthenprogramme effectiveness and long-term sustainability. At the global level, the Alliance operates through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), while governance modalities will be further refined during the inception phase. Currently, the Directors’ Meeting—comprising representatives from all 11 organizations—serves as the principal decision-making body for global planning and budgeting. Decisions are made through consensus whenever possible, or by a two-thirds majority vote when required

participating-org.narrative:
Stichting Amref Health Africa NL (formerly known as Amref Flying Doctors Nederland) is the Dutch branch of the African health organization Amref Health Africa. Founded to support healthcare development across Africa, the foundation raises funds, builds public awareness, and advocates for improved health systems. Its work focuses on training healthcare workers, improving access to primary healthcare, providing health education, supporting maternal and child health, and expanding access to clean water and sanitation.
The organization works closely with African governments and local communities to create sustainable, locally led healthcare solutions.
